title: What's a good first date?
old_caption: Planning a first date? Pick somewhere you can actually hear each other. A cozy spot, good food, a seat. Loud places can wait. Comfort beats fancy every time.

title: How long should I wait to text back?
old_caption:
Wondering how long to wait before texting back? There's no secret timer.
Reply when you can and mean what you say. Games just make everyone tired. Being clear is being kind.

title: Aquarius: the blind spot
old_caption:
Aquarius, going quiet when feelings get big is a way of protecting yourself. Try saying "I need a minute," then really come back.
Space is healthy when the other person knows you'll return.

title: Aquarius: what you need
old_caption:
Aquarius, you don't need someone who tolerates your quirks. You need a best friend who loves them, matching hats included.
Friendship first is a beautiful place for love to grow.

title: Aquarius: try this week
old_caption: Aquarius, this week try sharing a feeling instead of a theory. It doesn't need to be deep. "I felt happy today" counts, and saying it out loud lets people closer.

title: Aries: the blind spot
old_caption:
Aries, you decide in a second while they need a week. That isn't rejection, it's pace.
Kneel down, help with the shoelace, and run together. Patience is a form of care.

title: Aries: what you need
old_caption:
Aries, your fire is part of what makes you lovable. The right person warms their hands by it without fanning every spark into a fight.
Keep the glow cozy. Save this for the next time things heat up.

title: Aries: try this week
old_caption: Aries, this week's practice: ask one question, then let them finish the whole answer. No jumping in. Listening all the way through is one of the quietest ways to say you care.

title: Cancer: the blind spot
old_caption: Cancer, you hand out every bowl of soup and forget to keep one. Your feelings count too. Saying "I'd like some too" isn't selfish. It's how people get to care for you back.

title: Cancer: what you need
old_caption:
Cancer, you deserve someone who remembers you like peaches and makes it safe to be soft.
Being tender isn't too much. The right person treats it like a gift.
